learning_objective: 🎯 Explore the incredible craftsmanship of one of the world's oldest urban civilizations, famous for its bronze casting, precise seals, and baked clay toys!

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Two major stone masterpieces were found: The 'Priest King' (made of steatite, wearing a trefoil patterned shawl) and the 'Male Torso' (made of red sandstone, showing a deep understanding of human anatomy).

Harappans were masters of bronze. They used the 'Cire-Perdue' (Lost-Wax) technique. The famous 'Dancing Girl' of Mohenjo-Daro, standing in the tribhanga posture with bangles up to her shoulder, is a prime example.
Baked clay was used by common people. The most famous is the 'Mother Goddess' figurine with heavy jewelry and a fan-shaped headdress. They also made toy carts, whistles, and animal figures.

Thousands of seals (mostly square, made of steatite) were found. They have animal carvings (like unicorns and bulls) and undeciphered script. The 'Pashupati Seal' shows a seated yogi surrounded by animals.
Harappan pottery was mostly wheel-made, painted red with black geometric or animal designs. They also mass-produced beautiful beads from carnelian, lapis lazuli, and gold for jewelry.

fun_activity.title: 🕯️ The Lost-Wax Concept
fun_activity.instructions: Carve a small shape out of a block of wax (or a candle). Imagine covering it completely in wet clay, leaving a small hole. If you bake it, the clay hardens and the wax melts and pours out the hole ('Lost Wax'). Now you have a perfect hollow clay mold to pour liquid metal into!

exam_tips: 📌 The 'Lost-Wax' (Cire-Perdue) process is a very common short-answer question. Learn the exact steps.
📌 Know the details of the 'Dancing Girl' (height: 4 inches, material: bronze, found: Mohenjo-Daro).
📌 On the Pashupati Seal, memorize the animals surrounding the central figure: an elephant, a tiger, a rhinoceros, and a buffalo, with two deer at his feet.
quick_recap: ⭐ The Indus Valley script found on seals remains undeciphered to this day.
⭐ Harappan art is highly stylized but shows an astonishing realism in anatomical details (like the Male Torso).
⭐ Toys like wheeled carts and movable figures show that Harappans enjoyed a playful, settled urban life.
